title: Networking & Auth Module Design Playbook — VPC, IAM, Cluster Outputs
body:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook captures the proposed interface and upgrade strategy for the networking + auth primitive modules we use in Private deployments (VPC and on-prem variants). It is intentionally prescriptive about variable/output naming, backwards compatibility approach, and cluster-level auth bootstrapping so downstream stacks (EKS/GKE/AKS and bare-metal kubeadm) can be composed consistently.

High-level goals:
- Single, minimal surface area per primitive: vpc, iam, cluster-bootstrap. Keep modules composable and provider-agnostic where practical.
- Stable outputs with explicit compatibility shims for older stacks.
- Upgrade plan that minimizes customer blast radius for breaking changes (major version bumps, deprecation periods).
- Clear test matrix for cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure) and on-prem (kubeadm/rke2) variants.

Constraints and assumptions:
- On-prem installs may have no cloud APIs; modules should support an "external" mode where resources are only references (no create).
- Private control-plane runs in customer's VPC; we must avoid implicit public NAT or cross-account IAM by default.
- Terraform v1.5+ constraint, provider versions pinned in root module.

Proposed module boundaries (high level):
1) network-shielding (VPC/subnets/routing): creates VPC or returns references when external=true. Responsible for: CIDR allocation, public/private subnet naming, NAT gateways (opt-in), flow logs (opt-in).
2) auth-bridge (IAM/service-accounts/role mappings): manages cloud IAM artifacts, and generates service account manifests/annotations for k8s clusters. For on-prem, emits a mapping object used by the cluster-bootstrap module.
3) cluster-bootstrap (EKS/GKE/AKS/kubeadm glue): receives VPC outputs and IAM artifacts then wires cluster creation (or bootstrapping) and returns cluster endpoints, kubeconfig refs, and managed identity bindings.

Variables (suggested canonical names and types) — keep names flat and prefer snake_case for consistency:
- vpc_cidr: string (default "10.100.0.0/16")
- private_subnet_cidrs: list(string)
- public_subnet_cidrs: list(string)
- enable_nat: bool (default false)
- enable_flow_logs: bool (default true)
- external_network: bool (default false)  # if true, module will not create resources, only accept 'external_vpc_id' and 'external_subnet_ids'
- external_vpc_id: string (optional)
- iam_sa_map: map(string)  # logical_name -> principal (cloud-specific identifier)
- cluster_name: string
- cluster_mode: string (one_of: "managed", "self-hosted", "external")
- kube_admin_secret_name: string (optional)
- tags: map(string)

Outputs (naming convention and semantics) — these are critical: stable keys, never delete, only add with clear deprecation notes:
- vpc_id: string  # cloud VPC id or empty for on-prem external mode
- vpc_cidr: string
- private_subnet_ids: list(string)
- public_subnet_ids: list(string)
- private_subnet_cidrs: list(string)
- flow_log_ids: list(string)
- iam_service_accounts: map(string)  # logical_name -> cloud_service_account_id (or empty string for on-prem)
- cluster_endpoint: string  # endpoint URL for managed clusters or empty for self-hosted
- kubeconfig_secret: string  # name of secret created (if any), else empty

Compatibility and upgrade strategy:
- Semantic versioning: patch = non-breaking fixes; minor = new optional outputs/variables; major = breaking change.
- Deprecation window: when removing or renaming an output/variable, mark deprecated in module for one minor version and emit a terraform plan-time warning via validation+local.
- Shim outputs: when renaming an output, keep old output name but mark as deprecated string and copy value. Remove only on major bump.
- External mode: adding external flags (external_network) should be minor changes; ensure default false to preserve current behavior.

Planned upgrade path for existing stacks (example):
1) release module v0.9.0 adding enable_flow_logs=true default and new flow_log_ids output (minor).
2) encourage customers to pin module to ~>0.9.0.
3) release v1.0.0 when removing legacy output 'subnet_map' in favor of 'private_subnet_ids' — include shim 'subnet_map' that mirrors 'private_subnet_ids' and warn in docs.
4) on major v2.0.0 remove the shim after 6 months.

Testing and validation matrix:
- Unit: terraform validate and terratest (Go) for each module variant.
- Integration: spinning ephemeral accounts/projects on AWS/GCP/Azure and a kubeadm cluster in CI (self-hosted runner) once per week.
- Backcompat tests: terraform plan with older root module pinning older module versions to ensure shims work.
- Chaos: simulate missing flow logs, external mode toggles, and IAM missing permission errors.

Example usage snippet (consuming module in a root stack):
module "network" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//network-shielding?ref=v0.9.0"
  vpc_cidr = var.vpc_cidr
  private_subnet_cidrs = var.private_subnet_cidrs
  enable_flow_logs = true
}

module "auth" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//auth-bridge?ref=v0.9.0"
  iam_sa_map = { "node-proxy" = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/node-proxy" }
}

module "cluster" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//cluster-bootstrap?ref=v0.9.0"
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name
  vpc_id = module.network.vpc_id
  private_subnet_ids = module.network.private_subnet_ids
  iam_service_accounts = module.auth.iam_service_accounts
}

Operational notes and TODOs (open items):
- TODO: define exact format for iam_service_accounts map across providers (cloud id vs email vs short uid).
- TODO: add automated deprecation warnings in root-module CI when root uses deprecated outputs.
- Consideration: expose a lightweight 'resource_audit' output that lists created resource ARNs/IDs for customer reporting. This must be opt-in for privacy.
- Action: create GH issue to pin provider version ranges and add prow job for provider upgrades (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/401).

Rollback and recovery guidance:
- Never apply a major module version bump in production without a canary environment.
- For on-prem where module created resources are limited, provide an 'import_map' helper that documents how to import existing infra into the module state.
- In case of incompatible change detected in plan, workflow should abort and alert responsible oncall via PagerDuty with runbook link.

Appendix: naming conventions and rationale:
- Outputs use snake_case prefixed by resource kind (vpc_, private_subnet_, public_subnet_) to reduce collisions.
- Avoid provider-specific naming inside outputs (e.g., avoid "aws_vpc_id"), use generic keys. If provider-specific metadata needed, add <name>_meta map.

Concluding notes:
This is an initial draft intended to converge quickly on a small, clear surface area for downstream stacks. The emphasis is on predictable outputs, safe deprecation patterns, and an easier path for on-prem customers to opt into external-mode. Feedback welcome — especially from SRE on observability outputs and from Solutions Eng on migration ergonomics.

Change log summary (draft):
- 2025-01-08: initial draft by Priya Sinha
- 2025-02-11: added upgrade plan and test matrix, noted external_mode semantics (Miguel Ortega)

Unresolved decisions to surface in design review:
- Should enable_flow_logs default to true? Pros: better security/forensics. Cons: added cost and potential customer pushback.
- Standardize on provisioned NAT vs managed NAT gateway approach for hybrid environments.

End of document.
